archetype.name: Pocket Passer (veteran spot starter)
archetype.definition: A big-armed, statuesque veteran who now wins, when he wins, by working the middle of the field from the pocket, with the legs that once padded his game largely gone.

report.headline: One ugly Week 9 start defines a backup season trending the wrong way
report.take:
Wentz is the Vikings' third quarterback as of late November. His 2026 is four appearances: a relief outing against Green Bay where he played 83% of snaps and threw three touchdowns, spot starts at Chicago and against Buffalo, and a 10%-snap mop-up in San Francisco. Kirk Cousins, not Wentz, started the last two games with Kyler Murray out, which says plenty about where the staff ranks him. On 78 dropbacks his line is bad across the board: -0.195 EPA per dropback (47th of 55), a 49.3% completion rate, and a CPOE of -10.43 that sits 8.9 points under the qualifier average.

The Buffalo game is the season. He went 8 of 25 with two interceptions, a lost fumble and -17.6 passing EPA. His bad-throw rate that day was 41.7%, his CPOE -30.7, and he held the ball 3.13 seconds while pushing it downfield (32% aggressiveness, 10.4 intended air yards) against pressure on 34.6% of dropbacks. That is a quarterback trying to make up for a sputtering offense with tight-window throws he no longer hits. Outside that game he was below average but functional: positive EPA in the Green Bay relief, and a rough but winning 9-3 grind in Chicago.

What the numbers hide is how narrow his working area has become. Over the middle he's at +0.118 EPA a throw with a 65% completion rate. Outside the numbers and beyond 10 yards the accuracy falls apart: 36.4% on intermediate throws, -0.254 EPA to the right. Only Jefferson and the tight ends have produced anything with him, Jefferson barely (0.026 EPA per target). The sacks (9.2% rate, 38.9% pressure-to-sack) aren't new. He was at 0.396 pressure-to-sack last year and 0.371 in 2022, and at 33 the scrambling that used to pay for them is gone: 5 rushing yards on 9 carries, and designed runs at -1.377 EPA.

The career gives the fairest baseline. Last year in Minnesota he posted +0.06 EPA per play, a 1.1 CPOE and 7.2 yards per attempt, the profile of a competent fill-in. This year's -11.5-point CPOE drop and 7.2-point jump in bad-throw rate are too steep to be pure decline on one season's evidence. They rest mostly on 25 throws against Buffalo, so expect his accuracy to drift back toward the mid-range. But he's now third in line, so whatever regression comes will show up in very few snaps.

strengths.title: Middle-of-the-field timing throws
strengths.body: Between the hashes he has been a different passer: 65% completions and positive EPA, with the CPOE near neutral. Those are rhythm throws to Jefferson and the tight ends where his size lets him see and drive the ball. It's the one area consistent with last year's competent version, so it should hold.

strengths.title: A recent track record as competent backup
strengths.body: His 2025 line in five Vikings games was respectable: positive EPA per play, a slightly positive CPOE and 7.2 yards per attempt, 20th in the league. That season is a better guide to his true level than the 2026 sample, which one game dominates.

strengths.title: Accuracy holds on third down
strengths.body: On third down his CPOE is essentially neutral and he completes 64%, far better than his overall marks. The catch is the 28.6% conversion rate against 7.5 yards to go on average: completions are coming short of the sticks. It's a modest positive on 25 attempts, not a calling card.

concerns.title: Accuracy outside the numbers collapsed
concerns.body: He ranks last of 45 in bad-throw rate, and his CPOE is 49th of 55, 11.5 points worse than last season. The damage is concentrated on intermediate and outside throws, where completions fall to around a third. Buffalo drives much of it, but even his good Week 1 carried a 26.3% bad-throw rate, so some of this is real age-related erosion.

concerns.title: Sacks without the scramble payoff
concerns.body: A 38.9% pressure-to-sack rate and a 9.2% sack rate are long-standing traits, not a 2026 blip; he was at 0.396 last year. Earlier in his career the legs bought some of that back. Now he scrambles on 2.6% of dropbacks for no first downs, and designed runs are a net loss, so the holding costs him without the creation that used to justify it.

concerns.title: Starts have been the worst of it
concerns.body: In his two starts he's at -0.384 EPA per dropback with no touchdowns and a -19.5 CPOE. His only real production came in relief against Green Bay, when defenses hadn't prepared for him. That gap, and Cousins getting the call ahead of him, makes another start unlikely without more injuries.

trend.note: He went from +5.2 EPA in Week 1 relief to a near-neutral Chicago start, then the -17.6 Buffalo collapse. Over his last three games he's at -0.37 EPA per dropback, 0.175 worse than his season mark, and the staff has since turned to Cousins and slotted Wentz third.

nextGame.headline: Third-stringer against Atlanta; a soft defense he likely won't face
nextGame.body:
As QB3 behind Cousins, who started Weeks 10 and 11, Wentz plays against Atlanta only in mop-up duty or after another injury. If he did get snaps, the matchup is soft. Atlanta ranks 17th in defensive EPA and 18th against the pass, 21st in sack rate, and allows the 27th-most fantasy points to quarterbacks. The Vikings' top-ranked defense against an Atlanta passing offense that ranks 30th, with Minnesota a 7-point favorite at -345, points to a game Minnesota controls, which is the only realistic route to late snaps for him.

Availability is what matters here. Kyler Murray is out with a hamstring strain, and Jordan Addison, a 92%-snap starter, is ruled out for this game after thumb surgery. Addison's absence wouldn't cost Wentz much, since their connection was negative (-0.302 EPA per target), but it thins the outside options. On Atlanta's side, linebacker Divine Deablo (78% of snaps) is out, which loosens the middle of the field where Wentz throws best.

keyMatchups.title: Depth chart, not the defense
keyMatchups.body: Cousins started the last two games with Murray out, and Wentz is listed third. His fantasy and real-football relevance hinges on a lopsided score or an in-game injury. Murray's estimated return date is this game, but that's an estimate.

keyMatchups.title: Atlanta hits but rarely sacks
keyMatchups.body: Atlanta gets hits on the quarterback at the 6th-highest rate but ranks only 21st in sack rate. For a passer who turns pressure into sacks this often, that's the kind of front he could survive. The hits would still test an accuracy that has wilted under pressure.

keyMatchups.title: Deablo out opens the middle
keyMatchups.body: Wentz's only efficient area is the middle of the field. Losing Atlanta's 78%-snap linebacker weakens exactly that zone. It matters only if he plays.

nextGame.watch: Whether Murray is cleared and where Wentz falls on the depth chart. Any snaps beyond garbage time would mean something went wrong for Cousins.

restOfSeason.body:
Expect Wentz to be a clipboard backup unless injuries pile up again. If he does start, the likeliest outcome sits between his 2026 starts and his 2025 form: accuracy should rebound from a sample dominated by one 25-attempt disaster, but his outside throwing and sack habits look more like age than noise. Per start, I'd project roughly 140-200 passing yards, 0.5-1.2 touchdowns, a completion rate in the mid-to-high 50s and EPA per dropback still below average.

What won't come back is the rushing floor that once propped up his bad passing days. What will regress is the red-zone and fourth-quarter efficiency, which rests on 9 and 10 plays. Minnesota's defense, top-ranked in EPA, keeps games manageable for any quarterback, which is his best friend if called upon.
swingFactors: Whether Week 9 accuracy was a one-off or decline

confidence.note: 78 dropbacks, one game dominates, and as QB3 his role is in doubt.
